content.text: No minimum purchase commitment or take-or-pay mechanic is imposed on Corio anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 2. Corio Customer Application Management Revenue: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
input.rationale:
The agreement meets the preferred position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap imposed on us (Corio). Our variable fees are pure usage/revenue-based — the Application Management Revenue share is a percentage of revenue actually invoiced to Corio Customers (p0157), excluding professional service and network access fees (p0159) and accruing only once a Customer goes live (p0160). Implementation fees are time-and-materials against an agreed Statement of Work with a stated cap (p0161), i.e. ordered services only. Seat volume is uncapped rather than committed ("SOFTWARE USERS: BuySite Hosted Edition: Unlimited", p0151), with unlimited Customer sublicensing (p0032) and unlimited MarketSite.net access (p0041). Maintenance and support is expressly elective in economic effect — it continues only "provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees" (p0055, echoed in the survival language at p0098), so we can stop paying rather than being locked in.

Two minor sub-elements noted but not flagged: (i) the five-year initial term (p0096) carries annual MarketSite.net access and maintenance fees with no termination-for-convenience right, but these are fees for a service actually made available on an unlimited-access basis rather than a committed minimum volume or take-or-pay, so the walk-away trigger is not met; and (ii) the "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" in p0158 is a threshold on a fee waiver that benefits us (the 3000 royalty-free user licenses), not a purchase obligation. Exhibit D's initial-customer and marketing items are expressly "non-binding" (p0198) and framed as commercially reasonable efforts (p0205), so they create no volume commitment either. No redline required.
